text:
Sarah (Support): Customer BrightPath reporting 403s when calling /v1/generate. They see 'invalid_api_key' in the body and UI shows "Invalid API key". Customer insists key is valid and on paid plan. Repro attached from their side.

Customer: BrightPath Inc.: Here's the curl we ran (sanitized key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hello"}'
```
Response (400-level):
```json
{ "error": { "message": "Invalid API key provided.", "code": "invalid_api_key" }, "status": 403 }
```
They say they were on the Growth plan and had quota left. They pinged billing and confirmed invoicing/plan looks fine.

Sarah (Support): Repro steps I tried in staging with a test account on Growth - couldn't reproduce locally. Adding logs from customer request headers they provided: X-Account-ID: bp-3421, X-Plan-Name: growth, X-Region: us-east-1.

Tara (SRE): Can you paste the full response headers? curious if there's an entitlement header from the gateway.

Sarah (Support): From customer logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 18:02:12 GMT
Server: redwood-api-gateway
X-Request-ID: req_0a7b9f
X-Entitlement-Reason: plan_quota_exceeded
```
Body still "invalid_api_key" though.

Julian (Payments): Whoa — X-Entitlement-Reason is plan_quota_exceeded. That header implies billing service returned a gating decision, but the response body code is wrong. Looks like middleware mapping issue.

Sam (Eng): Agree. We have a mapping layer that converts internal enforcement codes to user-facing errors. If billing returns ENFORCE_BLOCK then auth middleware should return { "code": "plan_blocked", "message": "Plan does not allow this request" } not invalid_api_key. Possibly the old mapping table defaulted to invalid_api_key for unknown enum.

Sam (Eng): Can someone grab the gateway log for req_0a7b9f? I want to see the enforcement payload and the mapping path.

billing-bot: Billing decision cached for account bp-3421 -> plan: growth, usage: 98%, limit: 100%. enforcement: BLOCKED, reason: QUOTA_LIMIT. Cache TTL: 30s.

Julian (Payments): The bot confirms enforcement BLOCKED due to quota. But why message says invalid key? Two hypotheses: 1) Enforcement plugin returns an HTTP 403 but the global error formatter applies the invalid_key template for any 4xx without a mapped code. 2) A legacy branch in gateway erroneously overwrites error.code when X-Auth-Result header missing.

Tara (SRE): I'm seeing a spike in requests hitting the enforcement cache around that minute (18:02). We recently shipped a change that toggles caching key from account_id to tenant_id; possible cache miss causes enforcement service to return default (BLOCKED) for a few tenants while billing is reading fresh state. That could cause false positives.

Sarah (Support): Customer says this happened intermittently across a 2 minute window. That matches cache race. They lost ~30 requests. They want remediation and assurance it won't happen again.

Sam (Eng): Immediate suggestions:
- Hotfix: change gateway error mapping so enforcement BLOCKED -> code: "plan_blocked" and clear human-friendly message. That avoids confusing UX with invalid key.
- Short-term mitigation: increase cache TTL or switch to read-through cache keyed by account+region to reduce collisions.
- Long-term: add metric that emits (enforcement_reason != user_error_code) so we catch mapping mismatches.

Julian (Payments): Also add a header that is safe for UI consumption: X-User-Error-Code: plan_blocked (so frontend can decide whether to show billing CTA instead of "invalid key" flow).

Tara (SRE): I'll open an incident-runbook entry. Immediate action I can take: revert the caching key change we rolled out last night and roll it back to account_id to stop the race. Rolling back now will take ~5 minutes and will cause a short spike in enforcement calls. Anyone object?

Sam (Eng): No objections. I'll prepare a tiny patch for the mapping change and a unit test to prevent regressions. Patch and deploy to gateway staging, then to prod behind a canary.

Sarah (Support): Meanwhile I'll reply to the customer: explain this is a billing enforcement race that produced a misleading "invalid key" message, apologise, and say we're rolling back cache change and pushing a mapping hotfix. Offer to whitelist their account from enforcement for the window if they need immediate resume.

Customer: BrightPath Inc.: Please whitelist bp-3421 for 60 minutes if possible — they can't afford the interruption.

Julian (Payments): I can issue a temporary bypass token for bp-3421 for 60 minutes. Doing that now -> bypass-token: bypass-60-bp-3421 (will be logged).

billing-bot: Temporary bypass granted for bp-3421 until Tue, 10 Mar 2026 19:03:00 GMT.

Tara (SRE): Rolling back cache change now (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-10-rollback). ETA 4m.

Sam (Eng): Mapping patch created: PR #4281. Description: "Return explicit plan_blocked error for enforcement responses; add test to prevent defaulting to invalid_api_key." Will trigger CI and then canary deploy to gateway.

Sarah (Support): I've messaged the customer with the update and asked them to confirm once they can resume calls. Will update thread when they confirm. :thumbsup:

(30 mins later)
Customer: BrightPath Inc.: Confirmed calls resumed, labels now show proper message in our logs and UI shows "Plan quota exceeded" with billing CTA. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Sam (Eng): Closing notes for postmortem:
- Root cause: caching key change introduced tenant-level collisions causing enforcement service to return default BLOCKED for impacted tenant IDs.
- Secondary issue: gateway error mapping defaulted to invalid_api_key for unmapped enforcement enum values -> confusing customer UX.
- Actions: revert caching change (done), deploy mapping patch (PR #4281 merged), add integration test ensuring enforcement->user_error mapping, emit metric for mapping mismatches, add X-User-Error-Code header.

Julian (Payments): Follow-up: I'll open support-runbook checklist to include steps for temporary bypass and who to page for bypass requests.

Tara (SRE): I'll file the postmortem and link to PRs and rollback. Tagging oncall if we need to run RCA meeting.

Sarah (Support): Thanks team. I'm closing the escalation ticket and will attach the thread and postmortem links to the customer's ticket.

Sam (Eng): Nice work everyone. :zap:
